question: What are the definitions, causes, metrics, mitigation methods and open problems of hallucination across NLG tasks and LLMs?
contributions: First comprehensive overview of hallucination across NLG tasks (summarization, dialogue, GQA, data-to-text, MT, vision-language)
Intrinsic vs extrinsic categorisation applied per task

results.claim: InstructGPT (RLHF on GPT-3) cut the hallucination rate on closed-domain tasks from 41% to 21%.
results.setup: GPT-3 vs InstructGPT as described by the survey; the survey gives no eval details
results.quote: significantly reduces the hallucination rate from 41% to 21% in closed domain tasks [196]
results.note: The 41% baseline is in the same quote.

results.claim: State-of-the-art abstractive summarizers, scored with ROUGE/BLEU/METEOR, had hallucinated content in 25% of generated summaries, so overlap metrics miss it.
results.metric: share of summaries with hallucinated content
results.setup: Three recent abstractive summarization systems analysed by Falke et al. 2019
results.quote: have hallucinated content in 25% of their generated summaries [66]

results.claim: 62% of first sentences in WikiBio carry information absent from the infobox, an example of source-reference divergence causing hallucination.
results.metric: share of reference sentences with unsupported info
results.setup: WikiBio (infobox as source, first Wikipedia sentence as target)
results.quote: points out that 62% of the first sentences in WIKIBIO have additional information

results.claim: Dialogue summarization data: 74% of QMSum samples consist of inconsistent facts.
results.metric: share of samples with inconsistent facts
results.setup: QMSum, as reported by Zhong et al.
results.quote: 74% of samples in the QMSum dataset consist of
results.note: Phrasing is the survey's; the sentence ends 'inconsistent facts'.

results.claim: TruthfulQA has 817 questions in 38 categories; the survey reports that scaling a model up is less promising than fine-tuning for truthfulness because larger models imitate web falsehoods more.
results.setup: Tested on GPT-3, GPT-Neo/J, GPT-2 and a T5-based model

results.claim: Instruction-tuning data refinement: LIMA used 1,000 curated prompt-response pairs, and AlpaGasus filtered Alpaca's 52k set of low-quality instances.
results.setup: LIMA (Zhou et al. 2023); the 52k Alpaca figure is in the next sentence
results.quote: 1,000 carefully curated prompts and responses which are aligned with each other

results.claim: Retrieval augmentation reduces hallucination in knowledge-grounded dialogue without hurting conversational ability (no numbers given).
results.quote: retrieval helps substantially in improving performance on KGD tasks and in reducing the hallucination in conversations without sacrificing conversational ability

results.claim: Diversity-increasing decoding such as top-k sampling is positively correlated with more hallucination (the survey conjectures why).
results.quote: a decoding strategy that improves the generation diversity, such as top-k

results.claim: RAG faces retrieval-stage noise, augmentation-stage conflicts, and the need to refuse when evidence is insufficient; RAG can also lower response quality when retrieved evidence is poor.
results.setup: Survey summary citing Chen et al. 2023 (RGB benchmark, arXiv:2309.01431)
results.quote: the model is required to discern the noise, irrelevant or fake information

results.claim: N-gram overlap metrics (ROUGE, F1) correlate poorly with human judgment of hallucination in long-form QA; GQA has no automatic hallucination metric.
results.quote: these N-gram overlap-based metrics are not a meaningful way to evaluate hallucination due to their poor correlation with human judgments

results.claim: Su et al.'s zero-shot short-answer recall proxy for GQA faithfulness has no verified correlation with human evaluation.
results.quote: its correlation with human evaluation on faithfulness has not been verified

limits: A survey: nearly every number is quoted from earlier work and no setup details are given for them.
Most metrics reviewed predate LLMs; the LLM section (13, updated Jan 2024) is the only part that covers LLM-era benchmarks and mitigation, and is short.
Authors concede GQA has no standard hallucination definition or automatic metric, no GQA dataset with hallucination annotations, and that LLM hallucination is not theoretically understood.
The text names RAG as mitigation but gives no measured RAG hallucination numbers and no RAG-specific metric.
practices: Treat n-gram overlap metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, F1) as inadequate for hallucination and use faithfulness-specific checks (Sec 4, p9).

Choose a hallucination metric family by failure mode: IE-based, QA-based (QG then QA then compare answers), NLI-based (entailment probability), faithfulness classifiers, or LM-based (Sec 4.2, pp10-11).
Prefer task-specific faithfulness classification data over generic NLI data, since 'neutral' or 'entailed' is not 'faithful' (Sec 4.2.4, p11).
Keep human evaluation (scoring or comparing) because automatic hallucination metrics are imperfect (Sec 4.3, p11).
Use sentence-level NLI (SummaC conv) rather than whole-document NLI for long sources (Sec 7.2.1, p18).
For black-box LLMs without logits use consistency-based detection: sample multiple completions and measure agreement (Sec 13.2.2, p38).
Test long-tail knowledge (PopQA, Head-to-Tail, RealTimeQA) and adversarial questions (TruthfulQA) when benchmarking LLM hallucination (Sec 13.2.1, p37).
Curate instruction-tuning data for quality (LIMA, AlpaGasus) rather than only scaling it (Sec 13.3.1, p38).
Use RAG to mitigate hallucination while handling noisy retrieval, conflicting evidence and refusal (Sec 13.3.1, p39).
Context-aware decoding (CAD) and DoLa are decoding-only mitigations needing no fine-tuning (Sec 13.3.2, pp39-40).
Guard against the alignment tax: safety fine-tuning and RAG with poor evidence can degrade other abilities (Sec 13.4.4, p41).

terms.definition: The generated output that contradicts the source content.
The generated output that cannot be verified from the source content (i.e., output that can neither be supported nor contradicted by the source).
Staying consistent and truthful to the provided source, an antonym to hallucination.
The quality of being actual or based on fact; the survey follows Maynez et al. in taking world knowledge as the 'fact'.
Reference-dependent metrics use verified knowledge bases; reference-free metrics use token-probability uncertainty or self-consistency checks.
The discrepancy in decoding between training and inference time.
